chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir narrated to him, from Abu Abdullah al-Sayyari, on the authority of Abi Yaqoob al-Baghdadi, who said: Ibn al-Sikkit said,
"Why did God send Moses, son of Imran, with his white hand, the staff, and the means of magic, and send Jesus with medicine, and send Muhammad with speech and eloquence?"

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to him: "Indeed, when God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent Moses (peace be upon him), magic was the dominant trait among the people of his time. So He sent them from Himself that which was not within their power to match, by which he nullified their magic and established the proof against them."

"And indeed, God sent Jesus at a time when incurable diseases had appeared and people needed medicine. So He sent them from Himself that which they did not have the like of, by which he gave life to the dead, healed the blind and the lepers by God's permission, and established the proof against them."

"And indeed, God sent Muhammad at a time when eloquent speech and rhetoric were dominant among the people of his time, and I think he added: and poetry. So He sent them from the Book of God, the Exalted, and its admonitions and rulings that which nullified their claims and established the proof against them."
Ibn al-Sikkit said: "By God, I have never seen the like of this day. So what is the Proof against the creatures today?"
He (peace be upon him) said: "The intellect, by which you recognize the truthful one about God and affirm him, and the liar about God and deny him."
Ibn al-Sikkit said: "This, by God, is the correct answer."
ai.seo_question: What is the role of intellect as the divine proof in the absence of visible miracles?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* illustrates the Shia concept of *Tawfiq* (divine facilitation), where miracles (*mu'jizat*) are contextually tailored to nullify the specific claims of the dominant class in each era—magic, medicine, or rhetoric. Imam al-Rida’s identification of *al-'aql* (intellect) as the contemporary Proof (*Hujjah*) underscores the Shia epistemological principle that rational capacity remains the enduring, accessible means to verify truth in the absence of visible miracles.
